01ARTWORK PREPARATION

Clear artwork makes the handoff easier.

Structure, versions, images and bleed: what to review before approval.

DISCUSSION GUIDEUpdated 13 OCT 2026

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

Artwork needs to match the agreed packaging specifications. Before finalising the design, discuss the structural reference and handoff requirements so everyone works from the same version.

01Agree on the structure and version02Confirm bleed with the print provider03Supply assets and approval references

In this guide
01Agree on the structure and version02Confirm bleed with the print provider03Supply assets and approval references

01

Agree on the structure and version

Identify whether a file is for review or already approved. State units, printed faces and areas related to cuts or folds. The structural reference used for production needs project-specific checking.

  • A consistent filename and version across the team.
  • Reviewed text, product codes and languages.

02

Confirm bleed with the print provider

Adobe advises confirming required printer’s marks with the print provider and setting up bleed and slug areas first. Ask how bleed, safe areas and structural lines should be supplied for this pack rather than applying one universal value.

  • Backgrounds reaching the trim and details near folds.
  • How structural lines should be separated or annotated.

03

Supply assets and approval references

Illustrator’s Package function can collect linked assets and fonts; check font-sharing permissions first. Include a viewing reference, while identifying separately which file is intended for production.

  • Linked assets and an agreed approach to fonts.
  • Named approver, approval scope and final version.

TAKE IT INTO YOUR BRIEF
